description:
ContactsBackend::supports_type<O>(&self) -> bool (and the analogous MailBackend, ChatBackend, etc. methods in canonical sibling crates) is a sync method with no caller/account_id parameters. The answer is global per backend instance.

JMAP-qz9v.30 documented this limitation in the contacts-server trait rustdoc. This bead tracks the workspace-design question of whether to extend the signature to:

  fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(
      &self,
      caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      account_id: &Id,
  ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send;

Real use cases that need this:
- Multi-tenant SaaS where some tenants have contacts disabled or behind a paywall
- Per-user feature flags (e.g. beta access to a new draft extension)
- Storage-tier gating (e.g. contacts available for paying users only)
- Account-type gating (e.g. shared address-book accounts that only support read methods)

Canonical mail-server has the same signature shape — propagation would touch every extension-server *Backend trait. Workspace-design call.

Open questions:
- Is the right layer here the JmapBackend supertrait (so the foundation handles all per-account capability advertisement) or each extension trait?
- Should the method return Result (storage-checked) or stay bool (fast path)?
- Is the right home for per-account capability gating at the session-capability-builder layer (outside the trait entirely)?

Pre-1.0 (workspace is 0.1.x), so signature breaks are cheap. Post-1.0 this would require a major bump.

P3 because no consumer is currently blocked by the limitation.
title: Workspace design: add caller/account_id to *Backend::supports_type<O> for per-account feature gating
